question: How did chargeback volume in Nov-Dec compare to the prior 3 months, by reason category?
text:
Chargeback volume rose about 59% in Nov–Dec 2025 compared with Aug–Oct 2025, and every reason category went up by a similar amount. The data ends in June 2026, so Nov–Dec 2026 hasn't happened yet. This uses 2025, the latest Nov–Dec available. Because the two periods have different lengths, I compared average disputes per month.

- **All categories together:** 574 disputes a month in Nov–Dec, up from 362 (+58.6%).
- **Consumer Disputes:** 333 a month, up from 210 (+123, +58.6%). This is the biggest category by volume.
- **Fraud:** 201 a month, up from 126 (+75, +59.5%). This is the largest percentage increase.
- **Processing Errors:** 40 a month, up from 26 (+14, +53.8%).

The numbers look artificial. Every month in Aug–Oct shows exactly the same count, and so does every month in Nov 2025–Jan 2026. Volume then drops back to the Aug–Oct level from Feb 2026. That points to a fixed seasonal multiplier rather than natural variation, so treat this as a clear holiday-season jump in the model, not a fine-grained trend.

tables.title: Avg Monthly Chargebacks by Reason Category: Aug–Oct vs Nov–Dec 2025

sql:
WITH p AS (SELECT reason_category,
 SUM(CASE WHEN month_end BETWEEN '2025-08-01' AND '2025-10-31' THEN dispute_count END)/3.0 AS aug_oct_avg_monthly,
 SUM(CASE WHEN month_end BETWEEN '2025-11-01' AND '2025-12-31' THEN dispute_count END)/2.0 AS nov_dec_avg_monthly
 FROM __d WHERE month_end BETWEEN '2025-08-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY 1)
SELECT reason_category, aug_oct_avg_monthly, nov_dec_avg_monthly, nov_dec_avg_monthly-aug_oct_avg_monthly AS change, (nov_dec_avg_monthly-aug_oct_avg_monthly)/NULLIF(aug_oct_avg_monthly,0) AS pct_change FROM p ORDER BY nov_dec_avg_monthly DESC
